newsitem.title: UK: London tea auction finds selective demand.
newsitem.headline: London tea auction finds selective demand.

text.p: Demand was more selective at its latest London tea auction, the Tea Brokers' Association of London reported on Monday.

Among landed teas, brighter and medium East Africans were generally 2 to 5 pence lower, sometimes more with quality. Plainest Africans were mainly unwanted. But the few bright Ceylons were sharply higher with competition.
There was good demand for offshores. Brighter Africans sold well at last levels, others were about steady.
